about: Word fixes shared by every reel: how the transcriber wrote a word, and how it should read.
They are laid in as the rough cut writes outputs/<job>.transcript.json, the script captions, the graphics plan and every format read. The raw transcript/words.json keeps what was heard.
"words": one word as heard -> the word it should be. Capitals do not matter, its punctuation is kept.
"phrases": several words as heard -> what they should read, for a name no single word can carry ("chat gpt": "ChatGPT").
"check": real words that are sometimes a mishear. Nothing is changed; each run lists them so someone reads them where they were said.

Two more tables take the same three parts and are laid over this one: _local/caption-corrections.json for words that are yours alone (never shipped, never updated), and projects/<job>/word-fixes.json for a fix that is only right in one video.
After a cut, flag-words.py <job> lists the few words worth reading twice; respell.sh <job> rewrites that job's script with the fixes as they stand, without touching the cut.

The mishears in your brand kit are written in here. An update keeps your entries, and yours win on a word both name. The entries that come with the engine are platform and tool names and the misspellings seen most in real reels.
